section.title: Cool Down (5 minutes)
Student Activity
section.para: Acetaminophen is a common pain reliever and fever reducer. Here is a graph showing the amount of acetaminophen, in milligrams, in an adult’s body at different times after they take a normal dose.

image.alt: Graph of an exponential function, origin O. time (hours) and acetaminophen (mg).

list.item:
What is the vertical intercept?
Answer: 1,000

What does it mean in this situation?
Answer: There are 1,000 mg of acetaminophen in the person’s body after taking the medicine (this is the dose size).

What fraction of the medicine remained after one hour?
Answer: \(\frac34\) of the medicine remained after 1 hour since \(\frac{750}{1000}=\frac{3}{4}\).

Write an equation that represents the amount of medicine, \(a\), after \(t\) hours.
Answer: \(a=1,000(\frac{3}{4})^t\)

section.title: Response to Student Thinking
Points to emphasize
section.para: If students are still struggling with writing equations to represent exponential growth or decay, highlight a few examples from cool-downs and use practice problems from this lesson to provide further opportunities to examine the meaning of \(a\) and \(b\) terms and to practice writing equations to represent exponential decay.
